title: Listening Responses
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Classify eight replies to a nervous teammate as paraphrase, clarifying question, reflecting feeling, advice, or judgment.

learningObjectives: The learner will classify eight replies to a teammate's statement as paraphrase, clarifying question, reflecting feeling, advice, or judgment, correctly placing at least seven of eight on the first attempt.
prerequisites: Active listening and its parts (paraphrase, clarifying question, reflecting feeling), advice, and judgment, from the section "Communication, Listening, and Conflict" in Chapter 13

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit an answer, get feedback with the reason, and review what was missed
keyQuestions: What does this reply do: restate, ask, name a feeling, steer, or judge?
commonMisconceptions: Giving advice is a way of listening
Agreeing with someone is the same as understanding them
A question is always a clarifying question
assessmentOpportunities: "Have you tried writing notes on cards?" Which kind?
Is agreeing with someone the same as understanding them?
Name the three kinds of reply that are active listening.

controls.name: Choice buttons
controls.description: commit an answer. A wrong first answer gives a hint and lets you choose again; only the first answer counts.

controls.name: Show definitions
controls.description: opens or closes the reference table. Reading it is exploration, not evidence.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: moves to the next item after feedback. On the results screen, Previous missed and Next missed step through what you missed.

controls.name: Play again
controls.description: starts a practice run with the items reshuffled. Practice runs do not change the first-run score.
